events.label: birth
events.text: Born in San Anton Palace, Attard, Malta, to Alfred, Duke of Edinburgh.

evidence.quote: Victoria was born on 25 November 1876 in San Anton Palace in Attard , Malta

events.label: christening
events.text: Christened at San Anton Palace by a Royal Navy chaplain.

evidence.quote: The princess was christened on 1 January 1877 at San Anton Palace

events.text: Family left England for Malta when her father became Mediterranean squadron commander.

evidence.quote: In January 1886 , shortly after Princess Victoria turned nine , the family left England

events.text: Family moved to Coburg, Saxe-Coburg and Gotha.

evidence.quote: In 1889 the family moved to Coburg
Alfred and his family therefore moved to Coburg in 1889

events.label: meeting
events.text: At aunt's funeral in Russia met first cousin Grand Duke Kirill Vladimirovich.

evidence.quote: In 1891 , Victoria travelled with her mother to the funeral of her maternal aunt Grand Duchess Alexandra Georgievna of Russia

events.label: meeting
events.text: Visited grandmother at Balmoral and met cousin Prince Ernest Louis of Hesse.

evidence.quote: Her visit to her grandmother Queen Victoria at Balmoral Castle in the autumn of 1891

events.text: Married Ernst Louis, Grand Duke of Hesse and by Rhine, at Schloss Ehrenburg in Coburg.

evidence.quote: married on 19 April 1894 at Schloss Ehrenburg in Coburg

events.label: award
events.text: Made Dame Grand Cross of the Order of St Catherine.

evidence.quote: Dame Grand Cross of the Order of St . Catherine , November 1894

events.text: Reportedly discovered husband Ernst's infidelity on returning from a visit to her sister.

evidence.quote: Her marriage to Ernst suffered a further blow in 1897

events.text: Supreme Court of Hesse dissolved her marriage to Ernst Louis.

evidence.quote: The Supreme Court of Hesse dissolved the marriage on 21 December 1901
Victoria Melita scandalized the royal families of Europe when she divorced her husband in 1901

events.text: Daughter Elisabeth died of typhoid fever at age eight and a half.

evidence.quote: Elisabeth died at age eight and a half of typhoid fever during a November 1903 visit

events.text: Married Grand Duke Kirill Vladimirovich in Tegernsee, without imperial approval.

evidence.quote: The couple married on 8 October 1905 in Tegernsee
Victoria married Grand Duke Kirill Vladimirovich in 1905

events.label: conversion
events.text: Decided to convert to the Russian Orthodox Church.

evidence.quote: decided to convert to the Russian Orthodox Church in 1907

events.text: Recognized by Nicholas II as Grand Duchess Victoria Feodorovna.

evidence.quote: In 1910 they moved to Russia , where Nicholas recognized Victoria Melita as Grand Duchess Victoria Feodorovna

events.text: Couple arrived in St Petersburg, Russia, after being allowed to return.

evidence.quote: in May 1910 , the couple arrived in St Petersburg
In 1910 they moved to Russia

events.label: award
events.text: Made Dame of the Order of Queen Maria Luisa.

evidence.quote: Dame of the Order of Queen Maria Luisa , 31 October 1913

events.label: petition
events.text: Signed letter with relatives asking Tsar to show leniency to Dmitri Pavlovich.

evidence.quote: When Rasputin was murdered in December 1916 , Victoria and Kirill signed a letter

events.label: arms
events.text: Inescutcheon for Saxony dropped from her arms by royal warrant.

evidence.quote: In 1917 , the inescutcheon was dropped by royal warrant

events.text: Returned to Saint Petersburg from Romania.

evidence.quote: Victoria returned to Saint Petersburg in February 1917

events.text: Couple boarded a train to leave Russia for Finland.

evidence.quote: They were permitted to board a train without incident in the first week of June 1917

events.text: Family moved to a rented house in Porvoo, Finland, after two weeks at Haikko.

evidence.quote: They were permitted to board a train without incident in the first week of June 1917
After two weeks in Haikko , the family moved to a rented house in Porvoo

events.text: Left Finland with Kirill and went to Germany.

evidence.quote: in the autumn of 1919 Victoria and Kirill left Finland and went to Germany

events.text: Family group moved to Zurich after reunion with her mother in Munich.

evidence.quote: the family group moved to Zurich in September 1919

events.label: event
events.text: Attended a Nazi rally in Coburg.

evidence.quote: She attended a Nazi rally in Coburg in 1922

events.label: event
events.text: Trip to the United States to seek support for restoring the monarchy.

evidence.quote: Victoria went on a trip to the United States in 1924

events.text: Daughter Maria married Karl, Hereditary Prince of Leiningen.

evidence.quote: Maria , her eldest daughter , married the head of one of Germanys mediatized families , Karl , Hereditary Prince of Leiningen on 25 November 1925

events.text: Couple moved to Saint-Briac in Brittany and bought a house there as permanent residence.

evidence.quote: In the summer of 1926 they moved to Saint-Briac on the Breton coast

events.text: Discovered husband Kirill had been unfaithful; devastated.

evidence.quote: was devastated when she discovered in 1933 that her husband had been unfaithful

events.label: illness
events.text: Suffered a stroke after attending a christening.

evidence.quote: Victoria suffered a stroke soon after attending the christening of her fifth grandchild , Mechtilde of Leiningen , in February 1936

events.label: death
events.text: Died after a stroke, while visiting her daughter Maria in Amorbach.

evidence.quote: She died on 1 March 1936

events.label: death
events.text: Death date given as 2 March 1936 in the lead infobox dates.

evidence.quote: 25 November 1876 – 2 March 1936

events.text: Daughter Kira married Louis Ferdinand, Prince of Prussia.

evidence.quote: The marriage of their daughter , Kira , to Louis Ferdinand , Prince of Prussia , in 1938

events.text: Remains transferred from Coburg to the grand ducal mausoleum in Saint Petersburg.

evidence.quote: on 7 March 1995
